blindSummary: Capital region: diplomatic bubble; a standing gubernatorial ban on public LGBT activities (2017-2019 legacy); at the June 2024 Pride attempt police blocked the march, activists read their statement and dispersed peacefully. blindSourceSummaries: An international human-rights organisation (Oct 2025): a leaked draft judicial package would amend the penal and civil codes with provisions threatening LGBT people — behaviour 'contrary to biological sex and general morality' and its 'promotion' (up to three years' prison, amending the indecent-acts provision); sharp restrictions on gender-affirming care (minimum age 25, onerous eligibility); potential charges against trans people, care providers, civil-society organisations and journalists; justified as protecting 'the family and public morals'.

A national LGBT rights organisation's annual report 2025, subtitled on the siege against LGBT+ people: hostility institutionalised as explicit state policy — presidency-centred targeting, the family-policy ministry as implementing body, religious-broadcast regulator and content restrictions on expression and artistic freedom, one LGBT+ organisation closed, digital-platform penalties and broadcast censorship; six violations of the right to life documented (three recorded as hate-motivated), trans people the most affected; no state hate-crime statistics exist so data rests on media reporting. Launched at a public event in the capital.
